A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Vid2World with the same authors and research objective. Text extraction and visual inspection of all pages, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RT-1 and CS:GO predictions, component ablations and Real2Sim policy-evaluation outcomes in Section 5, with additional generated examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original robot manipulation, game simulation, policy-evaluation and newly added RECON navigation results, including ablations and appendix visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces Mixed Weight Transfer, which initializes additional past positions using averaged weights, with Extrapolative Weight Transfer, which redistributes future-facing weights using local linear extrapolation. Masked Weight Transfer is also introduced. This revises a central causalization component; diffusion forcing and causal action guidance remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds RECON open-world navigation, representing 40 hours across nine environments with continuous translation-and-yaw actions. This extends the work beyond v1's robot manipulation and CS:GO domains; the earlier coverage and drawer-closing policy task remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds AVID as an evaluated RT-1 comparator; v1 cited AVID and borrowed other baseline results without reporting an AVID row. Navigation introduces comparisons with NWM, NWM + Ego4D and DIAMOND navigation variants in Table 1 and Figure 6. The earlier RT-1 comparators and CS:GO Fast/HQ comparator set remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds DreamSim and navigation protocols using 500 segments for four-second target prediction and 150 for autoregressive evaluation, with four history frames, sixteen predicted frames and 1/4 fps baseline conditions. The stated policy-evaluation sample count changes from 80 to 50 trajectories per policy. Reported RT-1/CS:GO splits and training budgets otherwise remain.

E4.justification: v1's three-row transfer/action-guidance ablation becomes a five-row comparison of Shift, Masked and Extrapolative transfer, with guidance varied for the latter two. v2 also compares navigation errors across rollout horizons and temporal rates, including context exceeding the training length. Earlier failure-case and counterfactual-action analyses are retained in Appendix D.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 Appendix C.6.1 reports five random-seed navigation runs with means and standard deviations, accompanied by uncertainty bands in Figure 6; Table 1 also includes uncertainty for NWM baselines. This does not establish increased runs for the retained robot/game experiments.

E6.justification: Reported Vid2World RT-1 autoregressive FVD changes from 21.0 to 18.5, while CS:GO FVD changes from 102.6 to 106.6 alongside the revised transfer method. DIAMOND-Fast/HQ FVD changes from 903.9/562.2 to 577.1/368.5 without an explained protocol revision. AVID, navigation, DreamSim and revised ablation entries are added. Policy success estimates change from 0.341/0.756/0.874 to 0.260/0.820/0.880, accompanying the reduced sample count rather than establishing same-setting gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix A provides a linear-sequence counterexample for Shift Weight Transfer, an ordinary-least-squares derivation of Extrapolative Weight Transfer, and Proposition 1 with a smoothness-based error bound and proof. v1 contains no corresponding theoretical analysis; its mixed-weight construction is superseded.

C1.justification: The central novelty and contribution claims about transferring passive video diffusion models into autoregressive, action-conditioned world models remain. v2 extends the claimed demonstrated applicability to navigation and explicitly argues that transferring action-free video priors can avoid costly cross-domain action-labeled pretraining.

C2.justification: v2 interprets navigation with a 20-frame context versus 16-frame training as temporal generalization and distinguishes NWM's single-shot prediction from Vid2World's accumulating autoregressive predictions. RT-1 non-autoregressive superiority is softened to 'superior or comparable.' Existing limitations concerning fine control, object identity, respawn randomness and computational cost remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the extrapolative implementation with kernel size 3 and m=1, p=2, newly identifies LPIPS feature networks, and documents RECON action encoding, splits and resizing. Most earlier implementation information is retained. However, Table 3 still lists 'Mixed weight transfer,' conflicting with the revised method description.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning through a data pyramid, contrasting model transfer with cross-domain action-labeled pretraining in NWM/iVideoGPT and action-free co-training in AdaWorld. References add works including AdaWorld, RECON, DreamSim and RLVR-World, while dropping works including BERT, Mineworld and Tesseract.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction, preliminaries, methods and experimental narrative, adding explanatory subheadings. Training/sampling pseudocode moves from the main text to Appendix B, theoretical material leads the appendices, and citations change from numbered to author-year style.

P2.justification: v2 adds data-pyramid and navigation figures, redraws the transfer and training diagrams, and merges the RT-1/CS:GO tables into a three-domain table with DreamSim and inference-type annotations. The policy chart and main qualitative panel are redesigned. Earlier appendix examples are retained with relocation and caption/display refinements.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the methodological and empirical basis of the paper through a derived transfer construction, more informative component controls, and navigation comparisons with seed-based uncertainty. These address important gaps in v1's mechanism justification and demonstrated generality. The gains outweigh the smaller policy-evaluation sample and remaining reporting problems, including the stale transfer label in Table 3 and unexplained DIAMOND FVD revisions. Updated scores do not establish uniform performance improvement.
